rules.sentence: Schistocytes, or fragmented RBCs, are characteristic of thrombotic microangiopathic conditions and reflect intravascular hemolysis (seeImage. Intravascular Hemolysis).
Teardrop cells, nucleated RBCs, and leukoerythroblastic features suggest bone marrow infiltration, while the presence of immature WBCs may indicate leukemia.

Nutritional deficiencies causing megaloblastic anemia manifest as hypersegmented neutrophils and macro-ovalocytes, which are large oval-shaped RBCs with reduced or absent central pallor, providing critical information about underlying hematologic disorders (seeImage. Macrocytic Anemia).
A comprehensive history plays a central role in determining the etiology of thrombocytopenia.
Patients with platelet counts greater than 50,000/µL usually remain asymptomatic, whereas those with platelet counts below 20,000/µL often present with spontaneous bleeding.
Oral purpura and gross hematuria warrant special attention, as they may precede severe hemorrhage associated with ITP (seeImage. Petechial Rash).[29]
Additional important conditions include systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, prior bariatric surgery, and a history of blood transfusion.
